extracted.intended_audience: registered or prospective investment advisers and their compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements under the Investment Advisers Act for Form ADV amendments, books-and-records maintenance, brochure delivery, record retention, storage, and related compliance obligations for investment advisers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excepted person definition
rubrics_metrics.description: "Excepted person" means a natural person who is a qualified client as described in § 275.205-3(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Impersonal investment advice definition
rubrics_metrics.description: "Impersonal investment advice" means investment advisory services provided by means of written material or oral statements that do not purport to meet the objectives or needs of specific individuals or accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place of business definition for investment adviser representative
rubrics_metrics.description: "Place of business" of an investment adviser representative means an office at which the representative regularly provides investment advisory services, solicits, meets with, or otherwise communicates with clients; and any other location held out to the general public as a location at which the representative provides such services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal office and place of business definition for adviser
rubrics_metrics.description: "Principal office and place of business" of an investment adviser means the executive office from which the officers, partners, or managers direct, control, and coordinate the adviser's activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assets under management — how determined
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine "assets under management" by calculating the securities portfolios with respect to which an investment adviser provides continuous and regular supervisory or management services as reported on the adviser's Form ADV (17 CFR 279.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: State securities authority definition
rubrics_metrics.description: "State securities authority" means the securities commissioner or commission (or any agency, office or officer performing like functions) of any State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amending Form ADV — when amendment required
rubrics_metrics.description: You must amend your Form ADV: (1) Parts 1 and 2 — at least annually within 90 days of fiscal year end and more frequently if required by Form ADV instructions; (2) Part 3 — at the frequency required by the instructions to Form ADV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual updating amendment timing and any additional frequency specified in Form ADV instructions must be followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing of Form ADV amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to paragraph (c), you must file all amendments to Part 1A, Part 2A, and Part 3 of Form ADV electronically with the IARD, unless you have a continuing hardship exemption under § 275.203-3. Amendments to brochure supplements (Part 2B) are not required to be filed with the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have a continuing hardship exemption you must file paper copies with the SEC via FINRA when required to amend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form ADV filing fees
rubrics_metrics.description: You must pay FINRA an initial filing fee when you first electronically file Part 1A of Form ADV and an annual filing fee each time you file your annual updating amendment; fees are non-refundable and the amendment will not be accepted until fees are paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission has approved the filing fees; FINRA will not consider an amendment filed until the fee is paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to Form ADV are reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Each amendment required to be filed under this section is a "report" within the meaning of sections 204 and 207 of the Act (15 U.S.C. 80b-4 and 80b-7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition rule for filing Form CRS
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisers registered (or with a pending application) prior to June 30, 2020 must amend Form ADV by electronically filing an initial Form CRS satisfying Part 3 requirements beginning May 1, 2020 and by no later than June 30, 2020.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information on how to file with the IARD is available on the SEC website (http://www.sec.gov/iard).

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal and original entry records requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a journal or journals, including cash receipts and disbursements, and any other records of original entry forming the basis of ledger entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: General and auxiliary ledgers requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain general and auxiliary ledgers (or comparable records) reflecting asset, liability, reserve, capital, income and expense accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order memoranda and transaction instruction records
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a memorandum of each order given by the adviser for purchase or sale of any security, any instruction concerning purchase/sale/receipt/delivery, and any modification or cancellation; memoranda must show terms/conditions, person who recommended and person who placed the order, account, date of entry, and bank/broker/dealer through whom executed when appropriate; orders entered pursuant to discretionary power must be designated as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cash and bank records requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep all check books, bank statements, cancelled checks and cash reconciliations of the adviser.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bills and statements records requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Retain all bills or statements (or copies) paid or unpaid relating to the business of the investment adviser.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial statements and internal audit working papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Retain all trial balances, financial statements, and internal audit working papers relating to the adviser's business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written communications retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Retain originals of all written communications received and copies of all written communications sent relating to: recommendations/advice; receipt/disbursement/delivery of funds or securities; placing/execution of orders (and confirmations/allocations/affirmations with date/time stamps where required); predecessor performance and performance/rate of return of managed accounts, portfolios, or securities recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: not required to keep unsolicited market letters and similar public-distribution communications not prepared by or for the adviser; if a communication is sent to more than ten persons, adviser need not keep names/addresses unless distributed to persons named on a list, in which case a memorandum describing the list and source must be retained. For transactions subject to §240.15c6-2(a), confirmations and allocation/affirmation stamps required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record of discretionary accounts and powers of attorney
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a list or record of all accounts in which the adviser has discretionary power; keep all powers of attorney and other evidences of granting discretionary authority or copies thereof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written agreements with clients
rubrics_metrics.description: Retain all written agreements (or copies) entered into with any client or otherwise relating to the adviser's business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertisement and communication retention rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep a copy of each advertisement disseminated (with limited exceptions for oral ads and certain compensated oral testimonials/endorsements), any notice/circular/article/investment letter/bulletin sent to ten or more persons (other than associated persons), and if a communication recommends a specific security without stating reasons, retain a memorandum indicating the reasons for the recommendation. Also retain questionnaires/surveys used to prepare a third-party rating included in an advertisement if obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For oral advertisements, may keep materials used in connection with the oral ad instead of a copy of the oral ad. For compensated oral testimonials/endorsements, may keep records of disclosures provided pursuant to § 275.206(4)-1(b)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of ethics records
rubrics_metrics.description: Retain a copy of the adviser's code of ethics adopted pursuant to § 275.204A-1 (current or within past five years), records of any violations and actions taken, and written acknowledgments required by § 275.204A-1(a)(5) for persons who are or were supervised persons within past five years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access person reports and related records
rubrics_metrics.description: Retain records of each report made by an access person as required by § 275.204A-1(b), a record of names of persons who are or were access persons in the past five years, and records of decisions and reasons approving acquisition of securities by access persons under § 275.204A-1(c) for at least five years after the fiscal year in which approval is granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brochures, brochure supplements, and Form CRS records
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep a copy of each brochure, brochure supplement and Form CRS, and each amendment or revision that satisfies Part 2 or Part 3 of Form ADV, any summary of material changes not contained in the brochure, and a record of dates that each brochure, supplement, Form CRS, amendment, revision, and summary was given to any client or prospective client who becomes a client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also retain documentation describing the method used to compute managed assets for Part 2A Item 4.E if it differs from the method used for regulatory assets under management in Part 1A Item 5.F.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorandum for presumed-material disciplinary events
rubrics_metrics.description: If a legal or disciplinary event is presumed material but is not disclosed in the brochure or supplement, retain a memorandum explaining the adviser's determination that the presumption of materiality is overcome and discussing the factors described in Item 9 of Part 2A or Item 3 of Part 2B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation for testimonials, endorsements, and third-party ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: Retain, if not included in the advertisement, the disclosures provided to clients under § 275.206(4)-1(b)(1)(ii) and (iii); documentation substantiating the adviser's reasonable basis for believing that a testimonial/endorsement complies with § 275.206(4)-1 and that a third-party rating complies with § 275.206(4)-1(c)(1); and a record of names of partners, officers, directors, employees, and affiliates as required by § 275.206(4)-1(b)(4)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance calculation and supporting records
rubrics_metrics.description: Retain all accounts, books, internal working papers, and other records necessary to form the basis for or demonstrate calculation of any performance or rate of return of managed accounts, portfolios, or securities recommendations presented in any dissemination (including copies of information provided under § 275.206(4)-1(d)(6)); for performance of managed accounts, account statements that reflect all debits/credits/transactions and worksheets necessary to demonstrate calculation are deemed to satisfy requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policies, procedures, and annual review records
rubrics_metrics.description: Retain copies of policies and procedures adopted pursuant to § 275.206(4)-7(a) (current or within past five years), records documenting the adviser's annual review of those policies and procedures per § 275.206(4)-7(b), and any internal control report obtained under § 275.206(4)-2(a)(6)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Records relating to political contributions and covered associates
rubrics_metrics.description: When providing advisory services to government entities or covered investment pools, maintain books and records listing covered associates (names, titles, business and residence addresses), government entities served or that are investors in covered pools in the past five years, all direct/indirect contributions and payments to officials/parties/PACs, and the names/addresses of regulated persons to whom the adviser provides or agrees to provide payments to solicit government entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contribution/payment records must be chronological and indicate contributor name/title, recipient name/title (including jurisdiction), amount and date, and whether contribution was returned under exception. Adviser required to keep these records only if it provides services to a government entity or covered pool investor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record of intended audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a record of who the "intended audience" is pursuant to § 275.206(4)-1(d)(6) and (e)(10)(ii)(B).

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy/cybersecurity-related records required by §248.30
rubrics_metrics.description: Retain written policies and procedures required by § 248.30(a)(1); written documentation of any detected unauthorized access/use of customer information and response/recovery actions required by § 248.30(a)(3); written documentation of investigations/determinations regarding notification requirements under § 248.30(a)(4) including basis for determinations and any DOJ delay documentation and any transmitted notices; written policies/procedures required by § 248.30(a)(5)(i); documentation of any contract/agreements entered under § 248.30(a)(5); and policies/procedures required by § 248.30(b)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Custody-specific recordkeeping requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If adviser has custody/possession of client securities or funds, include: a journal showing purchases/sales/receipts/deliveries (including certificate numbers) and all debits/credits; separate ledger account per client showing purchases/sales/receipts/deliveries and date/price; copies of confirmations of all transactions; a record for each security showing clients with any interest and amounts/locations; a memorandum describing the basis for determining whether a related person's presumption of non-independence under § 275.206(4)-2(d)(5) has been overcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Client-level portfolio transaction and position records
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisers rendering supervisory or management services must make and keep true, accurate and current records showing separately for each client the securities purchased and sold and the date, amount and price of each purchase/sale; and, for each security with a current client position, information from which the adviser can promptly furnish the name of each client and the client's current amount or interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proxy voting recordkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: For clients where adviser exercises voting authority, retain: copies of all policies and procedures required by § 275.206(4)-6; a copy of each proxy statement received (may rely on third party or EDGAR if undertaking obtained); a record of each vote cast by the adviser (may rely on third party with undertaking); a copy of any document created by the adviser material to the proxy voting decision or memorializing its basis; and copies of each written client request and any written response regarding how the adviser voted proxies for that client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adviser may rely on third parties to make/retain copies provided an undertaking to provide promptly upon request is obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Client identity coding permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Books or records may be maintained so that the identity of any client is indicated by numerical or alphabetical code or similar designation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows coded client identifiers in records where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record retention periods and location
rubrics_metrics.description: All books and records required under paragraphs (a) to (c)(1)(i) inclusive, and (c)(2) (except specified subparagraphs) must be maintained in an easily accessible place for not less than five years from the end of the fiscal year during which the last entry was made, with the first two years in an appropriate office of the adviser; partnership articles and similar corporate records must be maintained in the principal office and preserved at least three years after termination of the enterprise. Records under (a)(11) and (a)(16) have a five-year retention with first two years in an appropriate office from end of fiscal year during which last published/disseminated. Transition rules may limit preservation of certain pre-registration private fund performance records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special transitional preservation exceptions apply for advisers previously exempt from registration prior to July 21, 2011.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation when ceasing business
rubrics_metrics.description: Before ceasing or discontinuing business, an adviser must arrange for and be responsible for preservation of required books and records for the remainder of the specified retention period and must notify the Commission in writing of the exact address where such books and records will be maintained during that period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification must be sent to the Commission's principal office in Washington, D.C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Micrographic and electronic storage permitted with requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Records may be maintained on micrographic media or electronic storage media that meets the terms of the section, provided the adviser: arranges and indexes records for easy location/access/retrieval; promptly provides upon Commission request a legible, true and complete copy in stored format, a legible printout, and means to access/view/print the records; and stores a duplicate copy separately for the preservation period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For electronic storage, adviser must establish and maintain procedures to reasonably safeguard records from loss/alteration/destruction; limit access to authorized personnel and the Commission; and reasonably ensure reproductions of non-electronic originals are complete, true and legible when retrieved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with substantially similar books under other statutes
rubrics_metrics.description: Any book or record made/kept in compliance with §§ 240.17a-3 and 240.17a-4 (Exchange Act) or MSRB rules that is substantially the same as required under this section shall be deemed in compliance herewith.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single record that contains all information required under multiple provisions need not be duplicated to meet other provisions' requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of discretionary power clarifying exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The term "discretionary power" does not include discretion as to price or time of a transaction if the client directed or approved purchase/sale of a definite amount of a particular security before the order was given by the adviser.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-resident adviser record location and undertaking rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-resident advisers must keep, maintain and preserve copies of required books and records at a place within the United States designated in a notice, and must furnish the Commission a written notice specifying that U.S. address within 30 days; alternatively, a non-resident may file an undertaking to furnish true, correct, complete and current copies of books and records to the Commission upon demand, and must furnish such copies within 14 days after written demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Undertaking must be in form acceptable to the Commission and is binding upon the adviser and its successors; undertaking suspended while adviser maintains all records in the U.S. in compliance with Rule 204-2(j).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve state-required records upon registration with Commission
rubrics_metrics.description: Any investment adviser that registers under section 203 after July 8, 1997 must preserve, in accordance with this section, the books and records the adviser had been required to maintain by the State in which it had its principal office and place of business prior to registering with the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery of brochures and brochure supplements — general requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If registered under the Act, you must deliver a brochure and one or more brochure supplements to each client or prospective client that contains all information required by Part 2 of Form ADV (17 CFR 279.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of brochure delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver your current brochure to a client or prospective client before or at the time you enter into an investment advisory contract with that client.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual delivery and summary of material changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver to each client, annually within 120 days after fiscal year end and without charge, if there are material changes in your brochure since last annual updating amendment: either (i) a current brochure, or (ii) a summary of material changes offering to provide the current brochure without charge and providing website, email (if available), telephone number to obtain brochure, and IAPD web address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery of brochure supplement timing for supervised persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver to each client or prospective client a current brochure supplement for a supervised person before or at the time that supervised person begins to provide advisory services to the client; if advice is provided by a team of more than five supervised persons, deliver only for the five with most significant responsibility for day-to-day advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A supervised person provides advisory services if they formulate investment advice and have direct client contact or make discretionary investment decisions even without direct client contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt delivery after disciplinary-information amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver to each client promptly after creation of an amended brochure or supplement, if the amendment adds or materially revises disciplinary information (Item 9 of Part 2A or Item 3 of Part 2B), either (i) the amended brochure/supplement with a statement describing material facts, or (ii) a statement describing the material facts relating to the change in disciplinary information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions from brochure and supplement delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: You are not required to deliver a brochure to a client that is an investment company registered under the Investment Company Act or a business development company (if advisory contract meets section 15(c) requirements), or to a client who receives only impersonal investment advice for which you charge less than $500 per year. You are not required to deliver a brochure supplement to a client to whom you are not required to deliver a brochure, to a client who receives only impersonal advice, or to an officer/employee/related person who would be a "qualified client" under § 275.205-3(d)(1)(iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Wrap fee program brochure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If you sponsor a wrap fee program, the brochure required to be delivered must be a wrap fee program brochure containing all information required by Part 2A, Appendix 1 of Form ADV; any additional information must be limited to information applicable to wrap fee programs you sponsor. If another sponsor delivers a wrap fee program brochure containing all required information, you need not deliver your own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A wrap fee program brochure does not replace brochure supplements required under other provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple brochures allowed for substantially different services
rubrics_metrics.description: If you provide substantially different advisory services to different clients, you may provide different brochures so long as each client receives all information about services and fees applicable to that client.
